   - Several inline functions that were previously defined outside the conditional block have been moved inside it, ensuring they are only available when the configurations are enabled.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The primary relationship between the modifications is that they all pertain to the conditional compilation based on `CONFIG_TRACE_IRQFLAGS` and `CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING`. By moving `mark_lock()` and related variables and functions into this block, the code is cleaned up to avoid unused function warnings and to ensure that all related functionality is grouped together under the same configuration checks.
- The removal of `mark_lock_irq()` indicates a simplification of the code, as it was no longer necessary once `mark_lock()` was properly defined within the relevant configuration context.
- Overall, these changes enhance the maintainability of the code by ensuring that only relevant functions and variables are compiled when the specific locking configurations are enabled, thus reducing potential confusion and improving code clarity.
